html: The Ngalawangka are an Aboriginal Australian group of the eastern Pilbara in Western Australia, in the upper Ashburton and Fortescue country toward the desert. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Little is recorded about them. Their neighbours on the map are the Banyjima and Palyku to the north, the Yinhawangka to the west and the Wawula to the south. Iron ore mining around Newman later transformed this country.
